From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's package.** The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labelling are the Seller's framing, not an agreed protocol. Nothing in our file indicates Wattlebridge principals have "settled" or "cleared" any of these clauses, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) says no negotiation position or approval is included. I have therefore reviewed every item, including those marked [STANDARD]. The "market context" preamble is advocacy and should be given no weight; several of the positions below are seller-favourable even against that stated range.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A cap at or above 50% of price for general warranties (100% is a reasonable opening ask for a business with known unresolved exposures), with separate uncapped or price-capped treatment for fundamental, tax and specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%; counter at 100% of price, settle no lower than 50%. *Reason: with ~30% of revenue and ~AUD 3.2m of debt both unresolved at signing, a 20% cap does not reflect the risk the Buyer is absorbing.*

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 (~1.04%), excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis ≤ AUD 10,000, basket ≤ AUD 120,000 (0.5%), and a tipping (first-dollar) basket, with related claims aggregated to pass the de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 10k / AUD 120k tipping; do not accept excess-only. *Reason: an excess-only basket of AUD 250k combined with the AUD 25k de minimis would exclude almost every individual issue identified in DD (e.g. each AUD 110k Sandbar renewal) from recovery.*

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion for general warranties; all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties (covering two audit cycles); 7 years for tax; no limit (or statutory) for title/capacity; and the default rule reversed so limitations only apply where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months general and strike the "applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default. *Reason: the Seller's default rule silently drags fundamental, tax and indemnity claims into the 18-month window.*

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, capacity and authority warranties capped at 100% of price (or uncapped), with a 6–7 year or unlimited claim period, and outside the basket/de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. *Reason: if the Seller does not own the shares it is selling, recovering only 20% of the price is commercially unacceptable and well outside any market norm.*

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None stated. Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out from every cap, threshold, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert as a non-negotiable. *Reason: as drafted, the Seller's language would purport to limit liability even for fraud, which is both unacceptable and likely unenforceable — but we should not be left arguing enforceability.*

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 22 Sept 2026, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]).
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure limited to matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter disclosed"; general data-room and public-register disclosure deleted or confined to a specific indexed list; cut-off date and no post-signing updates affecting warranty claims.
- **Recommendation:** Strike general data-room/public-record disclosure; accept only specific, fairly disclosed matters. *Reason: blanket disclosure of a data room and all public records would effectively disclose against every warranty and hollow out the entire warranty package.*

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** No knowledge qualifier at all; if one must be given, confine it to actual knowledge of a named short list of deal-team individuals, of a specific matter, and exclude imputed/constructive knowledge and advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3; fall-back is actual knowledge of three named individuals only. *Reason: "discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that shifts the Seller's disclosure burden onto the Buyer's DD and duplicates the overbroad disclosure in SPA-N-006.*

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours"; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen consent as a hard Condition Precedent to Completion, satisfied only by unconditional written consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied (or waived), Seller "all reasonable endeavours/best endeavours" obligation, and no waiver except by the Buyer. Consider a price adjustment/escrow if Bluefen terminates within 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a CP with a conditions-satisfied test; add MAC/termination protection. *Reason: Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) and the Seller's own letter admits the consent and conditions are not in hand.*

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure para 3: not repaid, no discharge in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment and executed deed of release/discharge of security (including PPSR releases) delivered **at** Completion, funded out of the purchase price via a payoff letter in the funds flow; completion deliverable, not a post-Completion covenant.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require payoff letter and discharge as Completion deliverables. *Reason: on a debt-free/cash-free deal, the Buyer must not pay AUD 24m and then inherit an undischarged AUD 3.2m secured facility on the Seller's promise.*

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure para 5: conditional on Completion/continued employment; silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus all on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accrual impacts) treated as Transaction Costs/Debt-like items deducted from the price or paid by the Seller through the funds flow at Completion, with a specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Add to the funds flow as a Seller-borne deduction with a gross-up for on-costs (budget ~AUD 480–500k). *Reason: these are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company; left unaddressed, the Buyer pays them post-Completion in addition to the full price.*

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (cl 11.1). Disclosure para 4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on clearance of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180k shown as open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay; failing that, a specific indemnity covering loss of or defect in title to the SOW3 materials (including re-development, licence and third-party claim costs), outside the cap/basket/time limits.
- **Recommendation:** Require the assignment as a Completion deliverable and widen the indemnity to title/use of the IP. *Reason: the exposure is loss of ownership of developed IP, not the AUD 180k fee — an indemnity capped at the fee is inadequate.*

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 is "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure para 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notifiability unknown.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of the investigation (or a Buyer-approved plan) before signing; a specific indemnity for all costs of investigation, OAIC/affected-party notification, regulatory penalties, remediation and third-party claims, outside the general cap and basket, with a 6-year survival; plus a warranty that no other incidents exist.
- **Recommendation:** Specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity and pre-signing investigation update. *Reason: a possible notifiable data breach under the Privacy Act carries regulatory and reputational exposure that the Seller's own letter cannot yet quantify or exclude.*

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure para 8: silent on whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation of terms, timing and termination rights; any renewal committed or falling due pre-Completion to be accrued in Completion accounts/treated as a price adjustment, or a Seller covenant not to renew without Buyer consent between signing and Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Obtain copies and either accrue in the working-capital/debt adjustment or add a pre-Completion consent covenant. *Reason: split into three identical AUD 110k items, each falls below a AUD 250k basket, so the structure of the Seller's thresholds would make these unrecoverable.*

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Single regime: general, fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity claims all subject to the same cap, thresholds and 18-month limit (cl 12.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes: (a) general warranties – negotiated cap/basket/time; (b) fundamental/title – 100% of price, long survival, no basket; (c) tax – 100% of price, 7 years, no basket; (d) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark) – outside cap, basket and de minimis; (e) fraud – unlimited.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft cl 12–13 into separate schedules per claim category. *Reason: the "administrative simplicity" framing is a device to collapse every protection into the weakest regime.*

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced solely by the Company share register at DD-012; Disclosure para 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent ASIC company extract and PPSR search at signing and again at Completion; Seller warranties that the shares are fully paid, free of encumbrances and constitute 100% of issued capital; delivery of original share certificates (or declaration of loss), executed transfers and board approval of registration as Completion deliverables.
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and add the full title deliverables list. *Reason: a company-maintained register is not independent evidence, and the Seller is simultaneously trying to cap title claims at 20%.*

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" — i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, basket.
- **Buyer wants:** A full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, capped at price, 7-year survival, no basket); IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance and employee/contractor assignments, with the Ironquay matter addressed separately (SPA-N-011); tax and IP escrow or R&W insurance as alternatives.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open and table a standalone tax deed/indemnity and IP warranty schedule. *Reason: these items were never actually negotiated — the Seller has simply labelled them "settled" to pull them under the lowest-protection regime.*

---

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Completion mechanics (N-008, N-009, N-010, N-015)** – Bluefen CP, Riverlark discharge, bonuses and title deliverables go to whether the Buyer gets what it is paying AUD 24m for.
2. **Structural protections (N-005, N-006, N-007, N-014)** – fraud carve-out, disclosure scope, knowledge qualifier and category separation; without these, the warranty package has little value regardless of the numbers.
3. **Economics of recourse (N-001, N-002, N-003, N-004, N-016)** – caps, thresholds, time limits and separate tax/title regimes.
4. **Specific indemnities (N-011, N-012, N-013)** – ring-fence known issues outside the general regime.

Recommend the covering reply reject the "[STANDARD]/cleared" characterisation expressly, so there is no later argument that silence on those clauses amounted to acceptance.

- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes: (a) general warranties – negotiated cap/basket/time; (b) fundamental/title – 100% of price, long survival, no basket; (c) tax – 100% of price, 7 years, no basket; (d) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark) – outside cap, basket and de minimis; (e) fraud – unlimited.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft cl 12–13 into separate schedules per claim category. *Reason: the "administrative simplicity" framing is a device to collapse every protection into the weakest regime.*

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced solely by the Company share register at DD-012; Disclosure para 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent ASIC company extract and PPSR search at signing and again at Completion; Seller warranties that the shares are fully paid, free of encumbrances and constitute 100% of issued capital; delivery of original share certificates (or declaration of loss), executed transfers and board approval of registration as Completion deliverables.
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and add the full title deliverables list. *Reason: a company-maintained register is not independent evidence, and the Seller is simultaneously trying to cap title claims at 20%.*

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" — i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, basket.
- **Buyer wants:** A full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, capped at price, 7-year survival, no basket); IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance and employee/contractor assignments, with the Ironquay matter addressed separately (SPA-N-011); tax and IP escrow or R&W insurance as alternatives.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open and table a standalone tax deed/indemnity and IP warranty schedule. *Reason: these items were never actually negotiated — the Seller has simply labelled them "settled" to pull them under the lowest-protection regime.*

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Completion mechanics (N-008, N-009, N-010, N-015)** – Bluefen CP, Riverlark discharge, bonuses and title deliverables go to whether the Buyer gets what it is paying AUD 24m for.
2. **Structural protections (N-005, N-006, N-007, N-014)** – fraud carve-out, disclosure scope, knowledge qualifier and category separation; without these, the warranty package has little value regardless of the numbers.
3. **Economics of recourse (N-001, N-002, N-003, N-004, N-016)** – caps, thresholds, time limits and separate tax/title regimes.
4. **Specific indemnities (N-011, N-012, N-013)** – ring-fence known issues outside the general regime.

Recommend the covering reply reject the "[STANDARD]/cleared" characterisation expressly, so there is no later argument that silence on those clauses amounted to acceptance.
